name: Meatlagging
description: BCI community slang for the frustrating cognitive delay that occurs when your biological brain processing falls behind your neural interface's data throughput — the sensation of your meat-mind struggling to keep up with what your chrome already knows. First documented in the Deeplink forums around 2204 among heavy BCI users in Tier 2-3, it describes a specific dissociative feeling: your augmented systems have already processed and responded to something before your conscious awareness catches up. Severe meatlagging can cause momentary identity disorientation, and chronic sufferers describe feeling like a passenger in their own body. Colloquially extended to mean any situation where a person's instincts or emotions are slower than their circumstances demand.
cultural_impact: Meatlagging has driven demand for neural synchronization therapy services and a class of illegal BCI tuning mods called 'sync patches' that promise to close the gap between organic and augmented processing — a booming gray market with significant health risks. The term has also entered casual use as a gentle insult for anyone who seems slow to catch on to a situation.
key_figures: Dr. Ifeoma Strand-Petrov (neurologist who first clinically described the phenomenon)
locations: Strand-Petrov Neural Clinic, Tier 3 Medical Row
The Crawlspace aug-mod parlor, Tier 2 South
story_hooks: A courier whose job depends on BCI-assisted reflexes begins experiencing dangerous meatlagging after receiving a mandatory firmware update from their corporate employer — and suspects the lag is intentional.
A support group for chronic meatlag sufferers in Tier 2 becomes a target for a corporation selling a 'cure' that actually creates dependency on their proprietary sync software.
Someone is using a targeted meatlagging attack — a signal that induces artificial BCI-brain desync — as an assassination method, making victims hesitate at critical moments.
definition: The dissociative cognitive delay experienced when biological brain processing falls behind BCI data throughput; broadly, being emotionally or instinctively slower than a situation requires.
usage_example: 'I knew the drop was wrong before I could stop myself — full meatlag, my chrome had already committed while my gut was still catching up.'
spread: Common Tier 2-3 among BCI users; known but less used in Tier 1 (fewer quality BCIs) and Tier 4-5 (better hardware minimizes the issue); the casual insult meaning has spread broadly
